subject: Copywriting
title: The Tabloid Formula
description: A fast breakdown of The Tabloid Formula for builders.

hook.text: British tabloids perfected headline writing. The Sun's 'GOTCHA!' after sinking an Argentine ship sold millions.

buildup.text: Tabloid rules: short words, active verbs, emotional triggers. 'SLAMS,' 'FURY,' 'SHOCK'—each one a punch.

discovery.text: The alliteration trick: 'Super Saturday Scorcher.' Sound patterns make headlines sticky and fun to say aloud.

twist.text: Tabloid headlines distort as much as they inform. Studies show they shape opinions more than the articles.

climax.text: Online clickbait borrowed every tabloid technique, just digitized. The Sun invented BuzzFeed's playbook.

punchline.text: Tabloids wrote the rules. The internet just copied them.

quiz.question: Which technique makes tabloid headlines memorable?
options: Short words, active verbs, and alliteration
